entities.name: Alena Arzamasskaia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Alena Arzamasskaia, sometimes called the Russian Joan of Arc, was a famed female rebel fighter in 17th-century Russia, posing as a man and fighting in Cossack Stepan Razin's revolt of 1670 in southern Russia. Unlike Joan of Arc, who was fighting in the name of her king, Alyona was rebelling against her czar. She was an Erzyan female ataman under the leadership of Stepan Razin. A peasant by birth from the Vyezdnaya sloboda of Arzamas, she was an elderly nun ("старица") before becoming an ataman. She commanded a detachment of about 600 men and participated in the capture of Temnikov in 1670, before being burned at the stake.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alena Arzamasskaia's rebellion against her czar in 1670 had significant regional impact on southern Russia, influencing Cossack movements and peasant uprisings for decades to come.
